suite_name: M2 Real LIBERO Object · SmolVLA (NVIDIA L4)
hardware: NVIDIA L4 (24 GB, EGL) · PyTorch 2.10.0+cu128 · LeRobot 0.4.4 · MuJoCo 3.3.7
notes: Measured closed-loop LIBERO Object Task 0 ('pick the alphabet soup and place it in the basket') against isolated lerobot/smolvla_libero policy server. Baseline BF16 succeeds in 139 steps; Lighting Shift (-42% luma) succeeds in 128 steps; Object Nudge (+12cm X, -8cm Y at step 20) fails (280-step timeout); INT8 weight quantization (125 linear layers) + 2 denoise steps achieves 2.86x lower latency (120.4 ms vs 381.4 ms) while keeping 139-step success.

replays.title: Real LIBERO · Baseline (PASS 139 steps) vs Object Nudge (FAIL 280 steps)
replays.prompt: pick the alphabet soup and place it in the basket
replays.failure_note: At step 20, translating alphabet_soup_1 by (+0.12m, -0.08m) broke closed-loop recovery: the arm repeatedly missed the shifted soup can until the 280-step timeout.

replays.title: Real LIBERO · BF16 10-step (381 ms) vs INT8 2-step (120 ms · 2.86x Faster)
replays.prompt: pick the alphabet soup and place it in the basket
replays.failure_note: Per-output-channel INT8 weight quantization across 125 MLP/projection layers + reducing flow-matching steps from 10 to 2 cut inference latency by 2.86x (381.4 ms -> 120.4 ms) with identical 139-step task completion.

replays.title: Real LIBERO · Baseline (luma 105) vs Lighting Shift (-42% luma 61)
replays.prompt: pick the alphabet soup and place it in the basket
replays.failure_note: Dropping diffuse brightness to 0.18 at step 20 cut mean main-camera luma from 105.0 to 61.3 (-42%), yet SmolVLA remained visually robust and completed the pick-and-place in 128 steps.
